Future contributors lack a recorded rationale for why new structural checks belong in `_plan_clarity.py` rather than inline in each gate.

findings.finding: The proposed `src/rebar/_plan_clarity.py` is a premature abstraction: it provides AC-checkbox parsing for exactly two call-sites (gates.py and det_floor.py), which does not meet the Rule-of-Three, and it rebuilds functionality that is already extracted in `det_operator_attested.ac_item_lines` (the shared AC parser det_floor.p6_ac_quality already consumes). A fourth implementation of the same `## Acceptance Criteria` / `- [` scan loop is NIH relative to the existing extractions.
scenarios: The new module adds a fifth variant of the same parsing loop, making future divergence (e.g. a change to how wrapped continuations are handled) even harder to keep consistent across all five implementations.
A reviewer or maintainer discovering the new module must now understand five variants and their subtle behavioral differences.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the new `parse_ac_items` (with wrapped-continuation support) and `detect_sentinel_assignments` functions to `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_operator_attested.py` instead of creating a new module. Both `gates.py` and `det_floor.py` already import from the plan_review package indirectly; if the import direction is a concern (gates must not import plan_review), place the pure parser in a small `src/rebar/_plan_structure.py` stdlib-only leaf and import from there — but this only makes sense if a third call-site materialises.

The plan does not address this root-cause duplication; routing the new floor logic through a third module (`_plan_clarity.py`) compounds rather than resolves the NIH issue.

scenarios: If a future change is made to the clarity scoring heuristic, it must now be applied in three locations rather than two.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a one-sentence positive rationale in the Approach section explaining why `_plan_clarity.py` is a new module rather than an extension of the existing `det_operator_attested.py` leaf (e.g., separation of concerns: AC-structure parsing is a distinct concern from operator-evidence tagging, and co-locating them would conflate two unrelated lint families).
evidence: Plan Approach: 'Add one pure shared plan-structure helper' — no explanation of why a new module rather than extending det_operator_attested.py

det_operator_attested.py line 14: 'Extracted from det_floor (which owns the P1-P9 static floor) so that grandfathered, size-ceilinged module does not grow' — identical rationale would apply to a new _plan_clarity.py, but the plan does not articulate it
det_operator_attested.py is already a pure-stdlib leaf imported by both gates.py (via det_floor.p6_ac_quality) and det_floor.py — the exact same dual-surface wiring the plan needs
findings.finding: The Approach section describes the chosen mechanism (a new shared `_plan_clarity.py` leaf) but states no positive rationale for why this structure was selected — e.g., why a new module rather than extending the already-established `det_operator_attested.py` leaf that already serves the identical dual-surface wiring pattern for both `gates.py` and `det_floor.py`.
scenarios: An implementer choosing between extending det_operator_attested.py vs. creating _plan_clarity.py has no documented rationale to guide the decision, risking an inconsistent structural choice (e.g., a scope-creep addition to det_operator_attested that conflates two distinct concerns).
findings.suggested_fix: In the Approach section, add: 'A new `_plan_clarity.py` module (rather than extending `det_operator_attested.py`) keeps AC-structure parsing — a plan-shape concern — separate from operator-evidence tagging, a completion-verifier concern; the two leaf modules remain independently testable and neither grows into a catch-all.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether `_plan_clarity.py`'s AC-item parser is intended to *replace* `_count_ac_reset`, `_count_ac_items`, and `ac_item_lines` for all call sites, or only supplement them — and if supplement, document why consolidation is deferred rather than leaving the intent ambiguous.
evidence: `_count_ac_reset` in `src/rebar/_engine_support/gates.py` lines 49-62: iterates lines, finds `## acceptance criteria`, resets on next `##`, counts `- [` items.
`_count_ac_items` in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py` lines 155-169: same iteration pattern, comment explicitly notes it 'Mirrors gates._count_ac_reset'.
`ac_item_lines` in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_operator_attested.py` lines 25-37: same pattern, returns list instead of count.
Plan says the new module adds 'parses standard Acceptance Criteria checkbox items with wrapped continuations' — a fourth variant without decommissioning the three existing ones.
The plan's Scope section updates `gates.py` and `det_floor.py` to 'apply the result' but does not indicate replacing the existing local parsers with the new shared one.
findings.finding: The plan adds a fourth AC-section parser (`_plan_clarity.py`) without consolidating the three pre-existing near-identical implementations (`_count_ac_reset` in gates.py, `_count_ac_items` in det_floor.py, `ac_item_lines` in det_operator_attested.py). Although the new module is labeled 'shared', the plan does not route the existing callers through it, leaving four parallel parsers in the codebase.
findings.location: Scope section — `Add src/rebar/_plan_clarity.py for the shared structural parser`
scenarios: A future AC-format change (e.g., a new checkbox syntax) must be applied to four parsers instead of one, causing silent divergence.
The 'shared' label creates a false impression of consolidation: other callers will continue using the three incumbent parsers, not the new shared one.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) have `_plan_clarity.py` become the single authoritative parser and update `gates.py`, `det_floor.py`, and `det_operator_attested.py` to import from it (eliminating the duplicates), or (b) explicitly note in Scope that full consolidation is out of scope for this ticket and will be tracked separately, so the 'shared' claim is scoped correctly.

scenarios: Implementer must invent the `hard-floor result` structure ad-hoc, leading to a shape that one wiring site cannot cleanly consume.
A PR reviewer cannot verify correctness of the adapter logic without a spec.
